Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: No operational centralized government portal with national ID authentication was found as of early 2026. DPI Map records: 'Enables authentication via government portal: NA.' The Ministry of Interior website (macnibe.interieur.gov.dz and passeport.interieur.gov.dz) allows tracking of biometric document applications but does not function as a general government SSO portal. The November 2025 draft law on digital identity aims to create a national digital ID platform linked to biometric cards for e-government access, but this had not yet been enacted or deployed.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score (1/No) was correct as of the DPI Map's October 2024 snapshot and November 2025 draft-law reporting, both predating launch. Since then, the Council of Ministers approved the operational launch of the Dzair Digital Services portal on 25 May 2026, after two citizen pilot phases and cybersecurity validation by ASSI; President Tebboune inaugurated the associated National Centre for Digital Services in El Mohammedia on 5 July 2026. The portal's national digital identity layer, co-developed with the Ministry of the Interior and tied to CNIBE, is the gating authentication credential for all services on the platform. Score upgraded from 1 (No) to 2 (Yes).
revised_comments: Algeria operates a centralised digital services portal, Dzair Digital Services, developed by the High Commission for Digitalisation together with the Ministry of the Interior. The portal's national digital identity layer, linked to the biometric national identity card (CNIBE), serves as the gating credential for authentication across all services on the platform. The Council of Ministers approved the platform's operational launch on 25 May 2026 following two citizen pilot phases involving over 1,700 participants and cybersecurity validation by the Information Systems Security Agency (ASSI). President Tebboune inaugurated the associated National Centre for Digital Services in El Mohammedia on 5 July 2026. At launch the portal consolidates 52 public services across seven ministerial sectors, including civil status, justice, health, land registry and national solidarity.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are not publicly available. DPI Map records: 'Terms of data storage and sharing available: NO' and 'Data handling terms exist: NO'. While Law 18-07 (as amended by Law 25-11 in 2025) requires ANPDP declarations and processing records, no publicly documented data sharing framework, consent mechanisms, or data flow documentation specific to the CNIBE system was found. Searched DPI Map, Ministry of Interior website, ANPDP website, and Algerian legal databases.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score (1/Not available) reflected DPI Map's October 2024 snapshot, which is accurate as a narrow, CNIBE-specific assessment. Broader personal-data handling rules have since been strengthened and made public: Law No. 25-11 of 24 July 2025 (amending Law 18-07) introduces mandatory Data Protection Officers, records of processing activities, data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing (including biometric data), and a five-day breach notification requirement; Presidential Decree No. 25-320 of 30 December 2025 establishes a national data governance framework by data-sensitivity level; and the ANPDP publishes declaratory/authorisation procedures and has conducted enforcement inspections since 2024. No CNIBE-specific data-sharing agreement was found published, so the framework remains general rather than ID-system-specific. Score upgraded from 1 to 2 (Partially available).
revised_comments: Collection, storage and sharing of personal data — including the biometric data used in the national identity system — are governed by publicly available procedural rules under Law 18-07 as amended by Law 25-11 of 24 July 2025, together with Presidential Decree No. 25-320 of 30 December 2025, which sets out a national data governance framework defining handling requirements by data sensitivity across public and private sector operations. Law 25-11 introduces mandatory data protection officers, records of processing activities, data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing, and a five-day breach notification requirement to the data protection authority (ANPDP), which also publishes a declaratory and authorisation process for data processing and cross-border transfers and has carried out enforcement inspections since 2024. No procedural rules specific to the identity system's own data-sharing arrangements have been separately published.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: No specific digital ID regulation exists as of early 2026. DPI Map explicitly records: 'Regulation for digital ID: NO'. The existing CNIBE is governed by general identity legislation (Presidential Decree 17-143 of 2017) rather than a dedicated digital ID law. The November 2025 cabinet-approved draft law on digital identity and trust services would be the first such specific regulation, but it had not yet been enacted by the legislature as of the research date. Searched DPI Map, government sources, and official Algerian legislation databases.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score (1/No) was correct at the time the draft law was only cabinet-approved (November 2025) and not yet enacted. Verified that Law No. 26-02 was adopted by Parliament and promulgated on 17 February 2026 (Official Gazette No. 14, 18 February 2026), fetched directly from the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications. The law's Title IV is dedicated specifically to 'l'identification électronique' (electronic identification), separate from general civil-status/identity legislation, defining electronic identification, proof of identity, identification means and systems, and three assurance levels. Score upgraded from 1 (No) to 2 (Yes).
revised_comments: Algeria has enacted specific legislation addressing digital identity beyond general identification law. Law No. 26-02 of 17 February 2026, published in Official Gazette No. 14 (18 February 2026) following parliamentary adoption, sets general rules for electronic trust services and electronic identification. Title IV of the law defines electronic identification, proof of identity, electronic identification means and electronic identification systems, and establishes three levels of assurance (low, substantial, high). The law also creates a National Electronic Certification Authority to supervise trust services and electronic identification, replacing the 2015 electronic signature framework.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The CNIBE is widely accepted as proof of identity in practice (required for voting, banking, administrative services, and obtaining a certificate of nationality per Ministry of Justice guidance of March 2025). However, the DPI Map records 'Identity act codifies legal status: NO', meaning the identity legislation does not explicitly codify the digital/biometric card as having equivalent legal status to traditional proof of identity. The November 2025 draft law would grant electronic documents the same legal validity, but it had not been enacted. Searched DPI Map, identity legislation, and Algerian legal databases.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score (1/No) reflected DPI Map's October 2024 assessment and the then-draft November 2025 law. Law No. 26-02 has since been enacted (17 February 2026) and formally defines 'preuve d'identité' (proof of identity) and 'système d'identification électronique' in law; Article 111 presumes electronic identification means already in use (which would include CNIBE) to be reliable pending new technical criteria to be set by the national information-systems security body. This is suggestive of increased legal codification of digital identity, but no source was found explicitly stating that the CNIBE credential itself now has legal status equivalent to traditional identity documents for all purposes — the practical acceptance of CNIBE (banking, voting, nationality certificates) documented previously predates this law and rests on administrative practice rather than explicit codification. The mjustice.gov.dz source cited previously could not be re-fetched (HTTP 403) and was not independently re-verified this round. Given the ambiguity, this row is flagged for human review rather than asserting a score change; revised_value_code left blank.
revised_comments: The national biometric identity card (CNIBE) is widely accepted in practice as proof of identity, including for voting, banking, and obtaining certificates of nationality. Algeria's identity legislation has not been confirmed to explicitly codify the biometric card as having legal status equivalent to traditional identity documents, although the newly enacted Law No. 26-02 of 17 February 2026 formally defines electronic identification and proof of identity in law and presumes existing electronic identification means reliable pending further technical criteria.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No publicly documented regular security audits or independent third-party assessments specifically of the CNIBE system were found. Presidential Decree No. 26-07 of 7 January 2026 established a new cybersecurity framework mandating dedicated cybersecurity units in all public institutions with continuous monitoring and regular audits, but this is a new framework and its application to the CNIBE has not been publicly reported. In 2024, Algeria recorded over 70 million cyberattacks (Kaspersky). No independent security audit reports of the national ID system have been published. Searched government websites, security reports, and audit publications.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score (1/No) reflected the absence of publicly reported CNIBE-specific audits, alongside a newly-signed cybersecurity decree (26-07, 7 January 2026) whose application to the ID system had not yet been reported. Since then, reporting (via an Ecofin Agency briefing carried by ALGERIATECH.news and corroborated by other coverage of the same 25 May 2026 Council of Ministers session) confirms that the Information Systems Security Agency (ASSI, Ministry of National Defence) conducted cybersecurity testing and validation of the Dzair Digital Services portal — which incorporates the national digital identity layer tied to CNIBE — ahead of its launch approval. Law No. 26-02 (17 February 2026) additionally introduces a statutory periodic-audit regime for trust and identification service providers, to be carried out by the national certification authority, ASSI, or accredited auditors. Score upgraded from 1 (No) to 2 (Yes), medium confidence, as the confirmed audit activity relates to pre-launch validation of the portal/identity layer rather than a demonstrated ongoing annual audit cycle for the ID system specifically. The Kaspersky and JORADP sources originally cited did not support the original score on inspection (Kaspersky press page contained no Algeria-specific figures; joradp.dz is a generic portal redirect) and have been dropped in favour of the sources above.
revised_comments: The national digital identity layer underlying the Dzair Digital Services portal, which is tied to the biometric national identity card (CNIBE), underwent cybersecurity testing and validation by the Information Systems Security Agency (ASSI, under the Ministry of National Defence) ahead of the portal's operational launch, approved by the Council of Ministers on 25 May 2026. The High Commissioner for Digitalisation confirmed in May 2026 that the platform had completed design, development, validation and cybersecurity testing stages. Separately, Law No. 26-02 of 17 February 2026 introduces a statutory audit regime requiring trust and electronic-identification service providers to undergo periodic compliance audits conducted by the national certification authority, ASSI, or accredited auditors.
